Where the money goes: straight to the medical debt that surviving twice left behind — two cancers cost more than anyone tells you. When that's paid down, a cut starts going to the fight at large. Until then, every sticker helps this particular survivor stay ahead of it. That's the whole books.
I spent fifty years riding to die.
Now I ride to live.

This isn't a wellness brand. It's what's left after dirt bikes, VFX death sprints, ayahuasca in the Costa Rican dark, yagé nights with the Inga in Colombia, a prostate gone in 2023, and a radiation mask bolted over my face in 2024. The shaka is how my people say I see you. The ribbon is for everyone in it — the ones who've been through it, and the ones who witnessed it. Put them together and you get the whole story. And if you count the rays in the burst, one is missing. It stays missing — for the ones we lost.

Who's Fizzle

b. 1968 · Mission Viejo, CA

VFX artist in a past life. Metal caster, writer, and 2X cancer survivor in this one. I make stickers and bronze medallions for the people who show up — and I'm probably the guy handing you one in a dealership parking lot.

Cancer found me twice. Both times it took something — and both times it left something behind that fifty years of throttle never gave me. What that was is a longer story, and I'm writing it. Sign up below if you want it when it's ready.
